name: Waldo Cortes-Acosta
event: UFC Fight Night: Cortes-Acosta vs. Walker
summary: A Dominican heavyweight (17-4, age 35) and former pro baseball pitcher who started boxing and MMA at 24. He went on a run of three straight knockouts (Delija, Gaziev, Lewis) between November 2025 and January 2026, then lost decisions to Alexander Volkov and Curtis Blaydes. He now headlines a five-round main event against Johnny Walker on about nine days' notice after Sean Brady pulled out of the original headliner. He has never been stopped.

how_they_fight.Striking: A boxer first (Wikipedia lists a 6-4 pro boxing record). He works a jab and short, fast combinations, and calls himself a high-volume fighter (Cageside media day). Power is real: knockdowns against Brzeski, Spann, Delija, Gaziev (two) and Lewis in our data. Against Lewis he hurt him with a knee to the body, then dropped him with a short punch (Cageside). He likened the Lewis knockdown punch to a baseball change-up.
how_they_fight.Grappling: Mostly a striker. He has one submission win (2021) and a blue belt per Wikipedia, which also notes he had no wrestling background. He can wrestle when he wants: he took Robelis Despaigne down 3 of 4 times and held him for almost ten minutes (our data), and caught a Lewis kick for a takedown (Cageside).
how_they_fight.Defense: Never stopped in 21 pro MMA fights. All four losses were decisions. Two of them came against wrestlers who held him down: Marcos Rogerio de Lima (3 of 7 takedowns, about five minutes of control) and Blaydes, who took him down in R1 and twice in R2 and took his back (Cageside). Volkov out-landed him 88 to 54 in significant strikes, used his reach and low kicks, landed a head kick, and left damage around his eye.
how_they_fight.Pace & cardio: Finishes come early. Ten stoppage wins: five in R1, four in R2, one in R3 (2022). His last three UFC knockouts were R1, R1, R2. Seven wins went the full 15 minutes. He has never fought a five-round bout, and this is one. Against Volkov he seemed to slow late in R2, then found a second wind in R3 (Cageside).
how_they_fight.Fight IQ: Calm, measured jab work when ahead. Against tall, rangy strikers (Volkov) he struggled to close distance; against Blaydes he couldn't land much in R3 while chasing (Cageside). Active: five fights in 2025, including a two-day-notice win over Gaziev (Wikipedia).

patterns: Jab and fast combinations; looks for the knockout in R1-R2 (nine of ten stoppages came in R1-R2)
Stopped for the first time by Walker (R3, Nov. 2026); his other four losses went the distance
Loses to wrestlers who hold him down (de Lima, Blaydes) and to a longer striker who kept him at range (Volkov)
Will catch kicks and take the fight down if it's offered
concerns: Two straight losses; he was the favourite against Blaydes
Facing a longer opponent: Walker has a listed 82-inch reach to his 78 (LowKick, Wikipedia)
Short-notice camp for a main event
Loading up and missing big; Walker said he waited for the miss to counter
keys_to_beat: Use range and kicks like Volkov did; make him reach
Take him down and hold him there, as Blaydes and de Lima did
Drag him into rounds 4-5, where he has never been

news.text: Booked against Johnny Walker as the new main event of the Nov. 7 card after Sean Brady withdrew injured from his fight with Gabriel Bonfim (first reported by Laerte Viana).
SB Nation calls it a five-round main event and lists him as the No. 8 heavyweight.
Lost a unanimous decision to Curtis Blaydes (29-28 x3) at Noche UFC; Blaydes won with takedowns and back control. The crowd booed the low-action fight.
Lost a unanimous decision to Alexander Volkov at UFC 328 (30-27, 29-28, 29-28). He weighed 264 lbs.

Knocked out by Johnny Walker at 2:27 of R3, his first stoppage loss: lost R1 to leg kicks, won R2 with right hands and top position, wobbled Walker early in R3, then was caught by a question-mark kick, backfist and right hand off a clinch break.
